title: Function overload resolution and ambiguous matches
recap: Overload resolution prefers better matches, such as exact matches and then promotions over ordinary numeric conversions. If no unique best viable overload exists, compilation fails with ambiguity.
Inspect argument types rather than just their displayed numeric values. A float literal and an integer literal can select different operations even when both look like four.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice function overload resolution and ambiguous matches.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement scale(int) to return twice the input as double, and scale(double) to return 1.5 times the input. The visible tests also call scale with a char and a float: reason about which overload is selected by promotion. All values are small and finite.
hints: The two overloads intentionally have different factors.
A float promotes to double; no explicit cast is needed at the call.
